reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 8 files in the AUR repository and found them to be standard, benign packaging files (PKGBUILD, systemd units, sysusers, tmpfiles, install script, nvchecker config) with no malicious injections. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was solely due to API errors (HTTP 400) preventing it from evaluating 4 files, not due to any security findings. The openrouter report is advisory only. There is no evidence of supply-chain compromise or malicious code execution during build or install.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from the qwen model experiencing API failures (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to audit 4 of the 8 files, resulting in an 'inconclusive' overall verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe. The openrouter model is marked as advisory and does not count towards the verdict.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .nvchecker.toml, PKGBUILD, cli-proxy-api.sysusers, and cli-proxy-api.tmpfiles due to LLM API HTTP 400 errors.
learnings: When an LLM API call fails for specific files, the audit tool should either retry the request, fall back to a different model for those specific files, or clearly separate tool failures from security inconclusiveness so the overall verdict isn't unfairly penalized by transient API errors.
